title: Nagoya TV Tower
geometryBasis: The named OpenStreetMap envelope fixes center and orientation. Japan’s cultural heritage register gives the 35 m square steel span, 90 m observation deck and 178.7 m tip height. The operator gives the 100 m outdoor balcony.
sectionBasis: Two exact CC0 Qualla photos dated 4 April 2011 control the steel silhouette, deck and antenna arrays. The structural case study controls the 15–26 m lower block, crossed reinforced concrete arches and 135 m transition to the antennas.
limitations: The April 2011 photographs show the upper tower clearly. Trees obscure the lower building, whose glazed elevations and subdivisions are approximate and use documented levels and structural arrangement.

Steel bay subdivisions, antenna panel fittings, underdeck joists, equipment and balcony fencing are simplified. The 35 m leg spacing, 90 m and 100 m deck heights, and 178.7 m tip follow published dimensions.

The untouched GSI DEM5A field controls footing contact. The alternative Terrarium field was sampled before selection and showed a broad high area at the tower. The Japanese elevation field is the higher-resolution ground product and represents modern park grades.
